# Kanalo

> An Android TV and Fire TV player for a playlist the user already owns. Kanalo
> plays M3U/M3U8 playlists and Xtream Codes portals. It ships with no channels,
> no playlist and no content, and has no affiliation with any content provider.

Kanalo is a player in the same category as VLC: it carries no media and offers
no way to discover any. The user supplies a playlist URL or portal credentials;
those credentials are stored on the device and sent only to that provider. There
is no Kanalo account and no Kanalo server, so the developer receives no user data.

## Facts
- Platforms: Android TV, Fire TV, Android phones and tablets. Android 7.0 (API 24) and above.
- Not yet available for iPhone, iPad or Apple TV.
- Price: free, currently in beta (version 0.9.4).
- Distribution: signed APK, sideloaded. Fire TV users install it with the Downloader app.
- Sources: M3U/M3U8 playlist URL; Xtream Codes portal; optional self-hosted companion server.
- Guide: XMLTV, including gzipped guides, with now/next and a full-day schedule per channel.
- Catch-up: Xtream timeshift, or an M3U catchup-source template. Kanalo never guesses a
  catch-up URL, so it does not silently play the wrong programme.
- Playback: Media3/ExoPlayer reads the provider's MPEG-TS directly — no transcoding and no relay.
- Live latency: Xtream providers answer a live .ts request with a backlog dumped at line speed
  (measured: 24 seconds of video in about one second) before settling to real time. A progressive
  stream cannot be seeked, so a player starting at the first byte stays that far behind live.
  Kanalo discards that backlog before playing and starts at the live edge. Delay beyond that is
  the provider's own pipeline, which no client can fix.
- Privacy: no telemetry, no analytics, no advertising identifier, no third-party data SDKs.

## Common questions
- Does Kanalo include channels or content? No. The app is empty until the user adds their own playlist.
- Does the developer see credentials? No. They stay on the device.
- Why does a stream buffer or fail? Nearly always the provider's upstream, which the player cannot fix.
- Is it legal? Kanalo is a media player and carries no content. What the user plays through it is
  a matter between them and their playlist supplier.
